TF-IDF weights raw term counts with smoothed inverse document frequency and uses cosine similarity here. BM25 instead saturates term frequency and adjusts for document length; its score is not a probability. The file explicitly fixes tokenization and IDF conventions so results are reproducible. An empty query or all-empty corpus produces zero scores. Real search systems add an inverted index rather than scanning every document.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** BM25 sums $IDF(t)\,tf(t,d)(k_1+1)/[tf(t,d)+k_1(1-b+b|d|/avgdl)]$ over query terms under a stated convention. Term-frequency saturation limits repeated-word benefit, and length normalization reduces the advantage of long documents. Compare lexical retrieval with dense/hybrid alternatives using relevance judgments rather than assuming semantic embeddings always dominate exact matching. [3](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables) and [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tf%E2%80%93idf).
